verdict.rationale: The core PlayCanvas Engine is confirmed MIT-licensed and open source ('MIT engine runtime' in playcanvas-probe-rt-2; community confirms 'the engine is open source' in playcanvas-comm-11 and playcanvas-comm-16), meaning a studio can ship and monetize games without royalties or per-install fees on the runtime itself. However, evidence also shows the hosted Editor/collaboration tooling is a paid subscription (e.g., $15/month for private projects, playcanvas-comm-4), which is a studio-tooling cost rather than a revenue royalty, so it doesn't contradict the engine's permissive licensing but adds nuance. Missing for 10: explicit vendor documentation stating 'no royalties/no revenue share' policy and independent legal/community confirmation of unrestricted commercial use terms.
